pull.title: KAFKA-4094: Reclassify broker configs that have sensible defaults as MEDIUM importance
pull.body:
https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-4094

Too many broker configs are currently marked as HIGH importance,
making it difficult for users to identify the settings that truly
matter for their deployment. This reclassifies 15 server configs
from HIGH to MEDIUM, all have sensible defaults and rarely need
tuning in most environments.

Changed configs (4 files):
- `ServerConfigs`: background.threads, num.replica.alter.log.dirs.threads, early.start.listeners
- `SocketServerConfigs`: socket.send.buffer.bytes, socket.receive.buffer.bytes
- `ReplicationConfigs`: replica.socket.timeout.ms, replica.socket.receive.buffer.bytes, replica.fetch.wait.max.ms, replica.fetch.min.bytes, replica.high.watermark.checkpoint.interval.ms
- `LogConfig`: log.roll.jitter.ms/hours, log.delete.delay.ms, log.flush.offset.checkpoint.interval.ms, log.flush.start.offset.checkpoint.interval.ms

Configs intentionally kept as HIGH: broker.id, listeners, log.retention.*, log.roll.time.*, min.insync.replicas, auto.create.topics.enable, delete.topic.enable, unclean.leader.election.enable, queued.max.requests, num.replica.fetchers, leader.imbalance.check.interval.seconds, log.flush.interval.messages, log.flush.scheduler.interval.ms, log.flush.interval.ms, num.recovery.threads.per.data.dir, and others that are essential or affect data safety.

commit.message:
Narrow scope to 15 configs; keep 7 operationally critical settings as HIGH

Revert queued.max.requests, num.replica.fetchers,
leader.imbalance.check.interval.seconds, log.flush.interval.messages,
log.flush.scheduler.interval.ms, log.flush.interval.ms, and
num.recovery.threads.per.data.dir back to HIGH importance.
These configs have significant operational impact and deserve
prominent visibility in documentation.

issue.title: KAFKA-4094: Fix broker config importance labels

repository.name: kafka
repository.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

issue.body: KAFKA-4094 reclassifies broker configuration importance so the generated broker docs match the labels' intended meaning: * **HIGH** — a deployment has to choose this. There is no default you can ignore, or the default is not a real deployment choice (for example `log.dir` defaults to `/tmp/kafka-logs`). * **MEDIUM** — there is a usable default, and an operator may still want to tune it. * **LOW** — a subtle knob that should normally be left alone. Deprecated settings are included here. `ConfigDef.Importance` has no deprecated level; adding one would change the public enum and needs a KIP, so it is not part of this change. No maintainer left a confirmed classification on the Jira. The 2024 suggestion to mark `log.dirs` MEDIUM conflicts with the current essential-config list (`node.id`, `log.dirs`, `process.roles`, `controller.quorum.bootstrap.servers`, `controller.listener.names`), so those stay HIGH. Apache PR #22019 is still open and unmerged; it only moved a subset of socket, thread, and checkpoint settings from HIGH to MEDIUM. Trunk still had the mismatches below. Broker settings that are synonyms of a topic config already marked MEDIUM are aligned with that topic label (`log.segment.bytes` / `segment.bytes`, retention, flush, `min.insync.replicas`, `unclean.leader.election.enable`, `compression.type`, `message.max.bytes`, and so on). Socket buffer sizes are aligned with the client configs, which are already MEDIUM. ### LOW Deprecated settings, which should not be treated as something to set: * `broker.id` (replaced by `node.id`) * `group.coordinator.rebalance.protocols` * `log.cleaner.enable` * `remote.log.manager.thread.pool.size` Internal checkpoints, load buffers, and retry backoffs with defaults that almost nobody should change: * `early.start.listeners` (defaults to the controller listeners) * `unstable.api.versions.enable`, `unstable.feature.versions.enable` (internal) * `replica.high.watermark.checkpoint.interval.ms` * `leader.imbalance.check.interval.seconds` * `log.flush.offset.checkpoint.interval.ms`, `log.flush.start.offset.checkpoint.interval.ms` * `offsets.load.buffer.size`, `offsets.topic.compression.codec`, `offsets.retention.check.interval.ms` * `transaction.state.log.load.buffer.size` * `add.partitions.to.txn.retry.backoff.ms`, `add.partitions.to.txn.retry.backoff.max.ms` * `share.coordinator.load.buffer.size`, `share.coordinator.state.topic.compression.codec` ### MEDIUM Usable defaults an operator may tune, including the topic-config synonyms above: * Threads and request handling: `num.io.threads`, `num.network.threads`, `background.threads`, `num.replica.alter.log.dirs.threads`, `num.recovery.threads.per.data.dir`, `num.replica.fetchers`, `queued.max.requests`, `request.timeout.ms`, `socket.request.max.bytes` * Sockets: `socket.send.buffer.bytes`, `socket.receive.buffer.bytes`, `replica.socket.timeout.ms`, `replica.socket.receive.buffer.bytes` * Replication tuning: `replica.lag.time.max.ms`, `replica.fetch.wait.max.ms`, `replica.fetch.min.bytes`, `auto.leader.rebalance.enable`, `unclean.leader.election.enable` * Log defaults: `log.segment.bytes`, `log.roll.ms` / `log.roll.hours`, roll jitter, retention time and bytes, flush interval messages / ms / scheduler, `log.segment.delete.delay.ms`, `auto.create.topics.enable`, `min.insync.replicas`, `delete.topic.enable`, `compression.type`, `message.max.bytes` * KRaft timing and the legacy static voter list: `controller.quorum.voters` (the docs say not to set this when using dynamic quorums; `controller.quorum.bootstrap.servers` stays HIGH), `controller.quorum.election.timeout.ms`, `controller.quorum.fetch.timeout.ms`, `controller.quorum.election.backoff.max.ms`, `sasl.mechanism.controller.protocol` * Metadata log: directory override, segment size and time, retention, and snapshot bounds. `metadata.log.dir` is optional and falls back to `log.dirs`. * Group, transaction, and share coordinator timeouts, segment sizes, and thread counts that already have production defaults. `mirror.num.replica.fetchers` matches `num.replica.fetchers`. ### Left unchanged * HIGH: `node.id`, `process.roles`, `controller.listener.names`, `controller.quorum.bootstrap.servers`, `listeners`, `advertised.listeners`, `log.dir`, `log.dirs`. * HIGH: internal topic replication factor and partition count (`offsets.topic.*`, `transaction.state.log.*`, share-group state topic, mirror state topic), plus `transaction.state.log.min.isr` and `share.coordinator.state.topic.min.isr`. Topic creation fails until the cluster meets the replication factor, and the partition count should not change after deployment. * HIGH: `sasl.oauthbearer.expected.audience` and `sasl.oauthbearer.expected.issuer`, so the broker definitions stay aligned with `SaslConfigs`. They are security checks for OAuth validation, not general tuning. * `default.replication.factor` stays MEDIUM. For the usual topic-creation paths the controller value is what applies. Broker config HTML is generated from `ConfigDef` by `genKafkaConfigDocs` and is not checked in. No doc source lists these importance values directly. ### Testing * `./gradlew spotlessCheck` and `checkstyleMain` / `checkstyleTest` on the touched modules. * `BrokerConfigImportanceTest` locks the labels above, including the settings that stay HIGH. * Unit tests for `raft`, `server-common`, `share-coordinator`, `transaction-coordinator`, `group-coordinator`, `server`, and `storage`. `mirror-coordinator` has no unit tests. `RemoteLogManagerTest.testRemoteDeleteLagsOnRetentionBreachedSegments` failed once on a remote-delete lag metric (expected 2048, got 0) and passed on rerun. That assertion does not read config importance. Reviewer notes: the testing details above can move to a PR comment if this description is used as the squash commit message.
